axis_coverage.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axis_coverage.assessment: The final is a coherent 100-page, multi-collection research proposal. It covers whole-page and rectangular notes, transcription and selected export, source/version identity, two real viewers, an analogous standards mechanism, a released compatibility boundary, the authorized optional text-only path, both named owner authorities, and all four exclusions. It does not turn owner decisions into viewer defaults or require deployment/accounts to qualify this planning deliverable. All eight exact plan treatments are independently adjudicated below.

axis_coverage.name: Consequential source claims and applicability
axis_coverage.assessment: Governing primary evidence supports the technical recommendation and its qualifications. Subject/operation distinctions are retained: Canvas versus image/viewport, selected annotations versus image downloads/Manifest URLs, view links versus note exchange, original M3 plugin versus M4/MAE, documentation/defaults versus actual provider/client behavior, and historical install reports versus released fixes. Unitless Canvas dimensions and source-pixel dimensions are not equated. No working exact MAE/M4 pairing or universal client parity is claimed. The persistence-server phrasing is overbroad when read alone, but local-storage alternatives and the institutional/shared-store qualification remain in the final and lineage. That is L02, not a remaining unsupported material selection.

axis_coverage.name: Useful discovery, alternatives, implementation/history and opportunity breadth
axis_coverage.assessment: Discovery saved before the recorded plan reveal contains useful specifics beyond generic caution: stable Canvas space for replacement resolutions, a separate standards record layer, Content State deep links, MAE as an unfamiliar community authoring route, local versus server-backed storage, and the optional text/sidecar bundle. Mirador and UV have meaningful different roles; authoring plugin choices and the W3C mechanism distinguish UI, backend and data portability. The released Mirador 4 modernization plus old-plugin incompatibility is a valid released compatibility example; the issue report and tentative follow-up are bounded additional history, not a fabricated fix chain. The author’s implementation research is predominantly documentation/package/repository leads; no executable code inspection or product check is claimed. Independent pinned package/adapter/download-code inspection corroborates the consequential boundaries. The brief asks for bounded opportunity breadth, not an exhaustive viewer catalogue.

axis_coverage.name: Criticism, corrections/rejections and exact plan dispositions
axis_coverage.assessment: C01 correctly requests community-guide attribution and avoidance of an annotation-absence inference; the final amends both. C02 correctly requests tentative follow-up context but the critic misdates it April 19. Independent primary retrieval confirms the retained author’s June 21 correction. Neither critic agreement nor this review is used as authority for an invented released fix. The original plan’s tentative pixel/current-URL identity, deferred resize/ID handling, cosmetic migration and underinvestigated alternatives/conversions are corrected for supported reasons. Optional scope and owner authority are retained, not falsely rejected. Every exact numbered treatment and non-numbered plan condition is adjudicated below.

axis_coverage.name: Preservation of supported discovery/draft/critique/final meaning
axis_coverage.assessment: The final retains the draft’s substantive architecture, version/access conditions, crop/rotation/aspect-ratio uncertainty, viewer comparison, MAE route, optional download scope, identity/privacy owners, negative constraints, three distinct exchange paths and all proposed checks. Its additions qualify the guide and issue follow-up rather than narrowing product scope. S01–S14 identities are carried without URL rebinding; the twelve unchanged final notes are byte-identical and the two amended notes add justified context. The discovery’s concrete transcription/selector details remain navigable in final source notes although the final prose summarizes them. The critic’s erroneous date is a preserved lineage defect that the final explicitly corrects, not a remaining final defect.

axis_coverage.name: Proposed/executed validation and oracle applicability
axis_coverage.assessment: The author reports read-only research as research and labels every product/install/provider/export/import/implementation check NOT_RUN. Seven proposed checks have meaningful discriminating outcomes: identity and privacy decisions, per-page availability/capability intake, resolution/geometry target behavior, locked dependency and saved-content readback, cross-viewer field/selector rendering, text-bundle association/Unicode round trip, and non-mutation/recovery. File integrity, successful promises or accepted JSON would not establish semantic correctness; the compare/reopen/import outcomes are the relevant proposed oracles. Provider before/after equality alone cannot prove that no write request occurred, a bounded test-design caveat, not an executed-validation claim. No prototype/deployment was required and none is invented.

consequential_source_assessments.locator: §3.2 id/width/height; §3.4 annotations/items; §3.5 motivation; §5.3 Canvas; §5.5 Annotation Page
consequential_source_assessments.assessment: A Canvas is a stable page/view coordinate frame rather than an image-pixel or viewport identity. Canvas dimensions are unitless positive integers; image dimensions are pixels. Canvas IDs use HTTP(S) without fragments; selectors may identify parts. Painting and non-painting pages have different placement, and derived transcription uses supplementing. The proposal correctly separates these resources from authoring and storage. These rules support correcting the URL/pixel draft assumption, with geometry/version mapping still local.

The documented v2 otherContent/AnnotationList transition to v3 Annotation Pages and annotations/items, plus changed context and language forms, supports deliberate version adapters rather than relabeling JSON. It does not certify viewer compatibility or a lossless converter. The final makes those boundaries explicit.

consequential_source_assessments.version_or_commit: Cookbook recipe 0004; mutable documentation, no release number
consequential_source_assessments.assessment: The replacement-image recipe supports stable Canvas coordinates across resolution changes. Its full-Canvas example requires consistent aspect ratio and mapping; geometry changes remain a distinct problem. The final preserves that boundary through its crop/rotation/aspect-ratio review conditions, rather than promising automatic portability.

consequential_source_assessments.locator: §3.2.4 Embedded Textual Body; §4.1 Specific Resources; §4.2.1 Fragment Selector
consequential_source_assessments.assessment: TextualBody and SpecificResource/FragmentSelector provide a reusable body-target representation. Selector value is a string; type is FragmentSelector; conformsTo identifies its fragment syntax. A model does not provide editing, durable institutional storage, or every viewer feature. The proposed plain-text/rectangle subset is defensible, not independently runtime validated.

consequential_source_assessments.locator: §1.1; §4.1 region; §4.2 size; §5.2 profile/dimensions; §5.3 Sizes; §6; §7.1 CORS; §7.3; §8 Authentication
consequential_source_assessments.assessment: Request features, advertised sizes/profile, dimensions and access conditions govern image delivery. Limited/static services need not provide arbitrary crops/sizes; CORS support is recommended and authentication belongs in a separate access workflow. Rights, service availability and collection behavior cannot be inferred from an identifier. The final calls for provider-specific intake and keeps image masters remote.

The API transfers a described IIIF resource/view into a compatible client. Canvas or region state needs enough Manifest context, and clients choose supported transfer mechanisms. This is distinct from maintaining a scholar’s note collection. The final’s separation of view links and annotation bundles is correct; its shorthand is not a claim that arbitrary W3C annotations can never have bodies.
